jobs.occupation: Software Architect: Agentic AI & Java, SitaWare Insight
jobs.description:
_Are you passionate about building sophisticated AI agents that solve real world problems? Join our Agentic AI team within SitaWare Insight, designing multi-agent workflows in Java and Python that power critical decision-making and help our customers get the job done faster and safer.

The job

As Software Architect on this team, you will combine deep software architecture expertise in Java with strong LLM and AI engineering fundamentals to shape the technical foundation of our AI-driven solutions. You will define the technical vision and architectural strategy that enable our product, AI agents and multi-agent systems to scale, while also designing and implementing the software solutions that bring this vision to life.

In short, you can look forward to:

• Converting customer needs into robust software architectures for AI agents, multi-agent orchestration and RAG pipelines

• Designing and implementing AI agents, including tool definitions, action groups and knowledge base integrations

• Ensuring safe and predictable outcomes through human-in-the-loop design and guardrails, and building traceability and transparency into our AI-based solutions

• Writing production-grade Java code with full test coverage, structured logging and robust error handling

• Establishing and maintaining technology standards, and evaluating new technologies as they emerge

Joining the team

You will join a growing team within the SitaWare Insight program, close to 50 engineers, architects and testers across five Scrum teams, spanning Aarhus and Copenhagen. We are building a brand-new team around this role:

an architect, a data scientist, five to seven developers and a tester, working closely with our Product Manager and UX designer. Java is our primary backend language, and we also work in Python for our AI tooling, and we collaborate with researchers to give our LLMs geospatial situational awareness, the ability to understand tactical maps and follow events across an evolving timeline. If you enjoy figuring out how to make new AI capabilities work safely and reliably in a domain where the stakes are real, you will feel at home here.

Your Qualifications

• 8+ years of software engineering experience, including significant experience in a software architecture role, designing and specifying system structures, interfaces and dependencies

• Strong backend development experience in Java, and familiarity with frontend architectures such as Angular or similar

• Strong understanding of microservices architecture, message queues and system integration patterns

• Experience with Docker and Kubernetes, and a solid grasp of how these fit into system architecture and deployment strategy

• A proven track record of defining technical vision and architectural strategy that supports product scalability and evolution

• Solid software engineering practices, including testing, logging, observability and version control, along with the ability to establish technology standards across a team

For more senior profiles, we are also looking for:

• At least two to three years focused on LLM or AI systems, including architecting and overseeing the deployment of AI-powered applications in Java and Python

• Deep understanding of orchestration frameworks, RAG architectures, vector databases, embedding models, hybrid search and tool-use/function-calling patterns

• Experience designing multi-agent systems, including orchestration patterns such as routing, delegation, parallelisation and result aggregation

• Familiarity with LLM evaluation frameworks and metrics, such as relevance, faithfulness and hallucination detection, and how to build evaluation and observability into system architecture

You should expect around two to four weeks of travel per year, giving you the chance to collaborate across our Aarhus and Copenhagen teams.

Please note that you must be able to present a clean criminal record and have lived in a NATO and/or an EU country for the past seven years as we work with security-classified projects. Read more here.

jobs.occupation: Declaration of interest regarding PhD project: The Department of Psychology at University of Southern Denmark (SDU) is looking for applicants for a PhD fellowship within the field of philosophy
jobs.description:
Declaration of interest regarding PhD project:

The Department of Psychology at University of Southern Denmark (SDU) is looking for applicants for a PhD fellowship within the field of philosophy, with background in one or more of the following areas: philosophy of psychiatry, philosophy of emotion, phenomenology.
We are looking for a person with a relevant degree (M.A., MSc. etc.) in philosophy or a related field. Starting date is September 1st, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The position is fully funded, full-time, for three years. The PhD degree will be awarded by the Faculty of Health Sciences.

 

Research environment

The PhD student will be based in the research group of Applied and Interdisciplinary Phenomenology in the Department of Psychology, SDU, at the Odense campus. The research group develops, disseminates, and applies methods to support cutting-edge research into subjectivity and the nature of human experience. Current group members have backgrounds in philosophy, psychology, anthropology, neuroscience, environmental studies, and pain research.

The group directly supports the professional development of its members, most of whom are postdocs or PhD students. In addition to receiving support from the project team, the PhD student will be supported by the broader group to develop their research, presentation, and teaching skills, as well as other academic skills, including those required for organizing academic activities such as workshops and conferences and for successful grant-writing. The PhD student will therefore be provided with the requisite knowledge and skills for pursuing an academic career in Europe or abroad.

The PhD student will also be provided with a work computer and a dedicated workspace at the Department of Psychology.

 

Project description

The PhD student will be part of the project, Understanding Experiences of Mood Disturbances in Depression (DEPMOOD), led by Anthony Vincent Fernandez. The project is funded by Independent Research Fund Denmark and runs for four years, starting September 1st, 2026. The PhD student will join the project for the final three years, collaborating with the PI, a psychology postdoc, and several external partners in Europe and the US, including philosophers, clinical psychologists, and psychiatrists.

The aim of the project is to establish a taxonomy of the variety of mood disturbances experienced by people diagnosed with depression, providing more precise characterizations of symptoms than those currently offered by concepts such as “depressed mood” or “anhedonia”. The project combines philosophical and qualitative methods, and includes in-depth interviews with people diagnosed with depression. The PhD student will not be expected to carry out interviews, as these will be conducted by the postdoc and external project partners. The PhD student’s primary role will be to help analyze the interview data using a combination of qualitative and philosophical methods. Their PhD thesis will therefore be a theoretical contribution, but will build upon the project’s empirical dataset.

In addition to producing a thesis, the PhD student will be required to take a variety of short PhD courses, carry out an international research stay, and fulfil light teaching duties.

The PhD student will be provided with DKK 10,000 per year for travel. Additional funds may be available.

 

Qualifications

Before the start date of September 1st, 2027, the applicant should have a master’s degree in philosophy or a related field and total course credits equivalent to 300 ECTS. Typically, this is a total of at least five years of education combined between bachelor’s and master’s degrees, with 60 ECTS obtained for every full year of study.

The candidate should have a background in philosophy of psychiatry, philosophy of emotion, and/or phenomenology. Familiarity with qualitative research methods (especially analysis methods) is an advantage, but by no means required.

The candidate should be proficient in English. Proficiency in Danish or another Scandinavian language may be an advantage, but is not required.

For further information about the project, please contact:
Anthony Vincent Fernandez

Department of Psychology

University of Southern Denmark (SDU)

E-mail: afernandez@health.sdu.dk

Please note that while we are happy to provide answers to questions about the position and application process, direct feedback on application materials cannot be provided.

Applications must include (in English, or with a certified English translation):

 

• 
A letter stating the interest, motivation and qualifications for the project (max. 2 pages) - upload under “Application form”.

• 
Detailed CV, including personal contact information as well as any publications or presentations

• 
Certified copy of diploma and transcripts (Master’s degree in a relevant field). If the applicant is in the process of completing their master’s degree, they should provide transcripts along with a letter from their supervisor confirming expected completion of their degree before September 1st, 2027.

• 
Writing sample of maximum 10,000 words (e.g., publication, conference paper, selection from a master’s thesis). If the sample exceeds this length, please indicate which section should be read.

• 
A document listing 2-3 references, with contact information and a brief note about your relation to the reference. Note that reference letters will only be requested for candidates invited to interview.

 

At this stage, no project proposal is required. Candidates invited to interview will be asked to prepare a brief project plan.

Please do not use generative AI in the formulation of any application materials. The purpose of these materials is to gain a clear sense of you and your abilities.

Shortlisting and interviews may be used in the assessment process.
 

For purposes of evaluation and assessment, application materials may be shared with external members of the project team at Aarhus University and Amsterdam University Medical Center.

Further information about the PhD-study can be found at the homepage of the University.

Applications must be submitted electronically using the link "Apply now". Attached files must be in Adobe PDF format. We strongly recommend that you read How to apply for a position at SDU before you apply.

Incomplete applications and applications received after the deadline will neither be considered nor evaluated

 

Closing date January 15th, 2027

 

We expect to conduct interviews within two months of the application closing date.
Successful candidates will be asked to send an application to the PhD Secretariat, Faculty of Health Sciences, to be enrolled as PhD students.
 

The PhD programme will be carried out in accordance with Faculty regulations and the Danish Ministerial Order on the PhD Programme at the Universities (PhD order)

 

Salary and Working Conditions at SDU

PhD students employed at SDU are employed as PhD fellows according to the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations in public employment (AC) agreement.

Salary and any salary supplement are paid according to your seniority level and as negotiated with your union representative. The base salary (excluding 18.07% pension contribution) is DKK 374,912.98   per year.

The Faculty of Health Sciences at the University of Southern Denmark is one of Denmark’s leading faculties of health sciences. With nine departments, internationally top‑class research, and a broad range of health‑related study programmes, we contribute to developing the knowledge, treatments, and healthcare system of the future.

As an employee at the faculty, you become part of an ambitious and interdisciplinary environment characterised by high academic standards, strong collaborations, and excellent opportunities for professional development. The faculty has activities in Odense, Esbjerg, and Copenhagen. In Esbjerg and Copenhagen, strong academic communities provide the framework for research and education, while our modern faculty building in Odense brings research, education, and administration together under one roof and is directly connected to Odense University Hospital.

The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

jobs.occupation: Experienced Research Support Officer at the Department of Management, Society and Communication
jobs.description:
We are looking for a skilled, experienced and dedicated Academic Officer to handle administrative tasks related to a broad portfolio of EU and nationally funded research projects within the fields of Sustainable Development with particular focus on the agricultural and food sector.

The employment will be for the limited period of 3 years.

You will become part of an international research team, where we take pride in providing high-quality work to the department’s research environment. Therefore, the position requires that you are service-minded and can work in a structured way in a busy environment with many inquiries and a wide range of contacts.

MSC is located at Dalgas Have in Frederiksberg and has over 140 full-time employees working in research, teaching, and administration.

MSC has an extensive portfolio of externally funded projects that help strengthen the exploration and dissemination of new research ideas. Funding comes from various sources, including the Danish state, national and international foundations, EU funds, and collaboration agreements with other institutions.

If you are interested in learning more about the department and our research, you can read more here: www.cbs.dk/en/research/departments-and-centres/department-of-management-society-and-communication

Job Responsibilities

The primary tasks will include:

• Project management in medium and large EU and nationally funded projects, including project planning, research activities and coordination, budgeting, grant administration, reporting, and stakeholder coordination.
• Research proposal and application writing and assisting with the preparation of contracts and budgeting.
• Support for research activities in medium and large EU and nationally funded projects with focus on Food, Nutrients and Agriculture, and Climate Resilience.
• Translating complex research results into clear academic and stakeholder-oriented communication and societal impact reporting.
• Business model analysis, governance framework development, stakeholder engagement.
• Development, design and dissemination of research communication materials.
• Ad hoc tasks.

Qualifications

We expect you to have:

• A Master's degree in Communication and Business Studies or a related field.
• Experience with project management of several projects in a public institution, such as a Danish university.
• Experience managing the full lifecycle of EU and nationally funded research projects, from concept development and proposal submission through project implementation and research activities to final technical and financial reporting to the European CommissionSolid communication and collaboration skills in English as well as in German.n.
• 3+ years of experience working in EU and nationally funded research projects within the fields of Food, Nutrients and Agriculture, and Climate Resilience.
• Experience in collaborating with diverse partners, particularly local and national governments in Denmark.
• Experience in societal impact assessment and reporting.
• Experience in research communication and design (knowledge in adobe suite, website design and maintenance).
• Experience in circular business model and governance development.
• Experience in stakeholder engagement and community management across Denmark and the EU. 
• Experience in workshop design and event management.
• Experience with qualitative research (survey, interviews, market analysis, qualitative coding), and end-user engagement.
• Experience in supporting study activities and administrative course planning.
We value that you are:

• Independent, responsible, and service-oriented
• Organized, able to adjust, and solution focused.
• Structured, systematic, and detail oriented.
• Able to manage multiple tasks simultaneously and prioritize as needed.
• Skilled at building and maintaining good relationships with internal and external partners and colleagues.

Are You the One We’re Looking For?

If you can see yourself as our Research Support Officer, please send us your CV, academic diplomas and a short, motivated application describing your interest in the position and why you are qualified.

Salary and Terms of Employment

Employment and salary are in accordance with the applicable agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the relevant organization, with placement and salary depending on qualifications and experience. There will be an opportunity to negotiate personal supplements upon employment.

The position is 37 hours per week.

Recruitment Process

Copenhagen Business School invites all qualified candidates to apply. A hiring committee will assess the applications an ongoing basis and invite a selection of qualified candidates for interviews.

One of CBS’s strategic goals is to promote diversity and inclusion in our organization. Therefore, we strive for a recruitment process that minimizes potential bias. We encourage applicants not to include photos or unnecessary personal information in their applications.

We review applications and conduct interviews on an ongoing basis.

Further Information

For information about the position, please contact Project Manager, Assistant Professor Isabel Froes, ifr.msc@cbs.dk

For information about the employment process please contact jobcall.msc@cbs.dk 

You apply for the position online by clicking the “apply online” link, where you fill out the application form and attach your application, academic diploma(s), and CV.

Application due 11/5/2026

jobs.occupation: Head of Procurement and Stock Control

We are looking for a Head of Procurement and Stock Control to make sure our bakery always has the right ingredients and supplies, in the right quantity, at the right quality and at the right price. What you will do

• Monitor the raw material percentage by product group and report deviations to the Head Baker and management

• Prepare a stock plan for peak periods that covers the extra demand, and agree it with the Head Baker 

Who you are 

• Accurate, with a good head for numbers 

• Structured and a strong planner 

• Clear communicator with suppliers and colleagues 

• Good understanding of bakery ingredients and production

• Working hours: daytime hours, with one fixed weekday off and work every second weekend 

• Workplace: Strandvejen 213, 2900 Hellerup 

• Start date: 9 November 

• Salary: [to be agreed]

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral position in big data analytics in teen substance use at the Centre for Alcohol and Drug Research at Aarhus University in Denmark
jobs.description:
Applications are invited from early-career postdoctoral researchers who can demonstrate an established track record in big data analytics within the field of substance use. The two-year full time position will commence in February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. You will get the opportunity to analyse and publish on big data from a very large RCT examining out-of-the-box brain-based interventions for adolescents engaged in alcohol use. You will also get unique opportunities to examine risk and protective factors for substance use and related behaviors across large adolescent datasets. 

You will be working under the strong mentorship of Professor Kristine Rømer Thomsen at Aarhus University and Professor Sarah W. Feldstein Ewing (UConn Health, U.S.), and in close collaboration with other prominent researchers in the field. The Centre for Alcohol and Drug Research is part of the Department of Psychology and Behavioural Sciences at Aarhus University and provides a vibrant and stimulating research environment in the charming city of Aarhus.

About the applicant
We are thrilled to welcome individuals of any nationality to come live in Denmark and join the project. Appointment as postdoc requires scientific qualifications at the PhD level in a relevant field. You must be able to demonstrate a track record in big data analytics in, or closely related to, the substance use field, and the capacity to not only conduct advanced quantitative analyses, but also the capacity to easily communicate those analyses, e.g., chat with colleagues on the project; write up relevant analytics plans and output in English, including for high impact international journals. The data collection was recently completed, offering attractive opportunities to examine and publish on large datasets and be part of a nationally and internationally strong research team.

Who we are
Centre for Alcohol and Drug Research is an interdisciplinary social science research center. Our research focuses on treatment, prevention, policy, drug markets and recreational use. We study both legal and illegal substances. The Centre is interdisciplinary, and researchers have backgrounds in psychology, sociology, anthropology, criminology, political science and public health. Our task is to conduct research projects, provide education, disseminate knowledge about alcohol and substance use, and collaborate with national stakeholders as well as international research institutions.
See also www.crf.au.dk

The Department of Psychology and Behavioural Sciences is part of Aarhus BSS, Aarhus University – a top 100 university. Aarhus BSS has achieved the triple-crown AACSB, AMBA and EQUIS accreditations. 
At the Department of Psychology and Behavioural Sciences, we teach and conduct research into the most significant subject areas of psychology. The department employs around 55-60 academic staff members and 40 PhD students. Our researchers have a strong tradition for collaborating with Danish as well as international researchers from many different academic fields such as health and psychiatry, education, pedagogic, linguistics, philosophy, religious studies, organizational development and management, economics and neuroscience.
For more information about the Department of Psychology and Behavioural Sciences, please visit: http://psy.au.dk/en/

Further Information
Further particulars on the position may be obtained from Professor Kristine Rømer Thomsen, Centre for Alcohol and Drug Research, e-mail: krt.crf@psy.au.dk, Tel.:+45 2991 6092.

If you require assistance with uploading your application or have questions regarding the recruitment process, please contact: Charlotte Thomsen, HR coordinator, e-mail: charlotte@au.dk, Tel.: +45 8716 5362.

The place of work is Centre for Alcohol and Drug Research, Bartholins Allé 11, 8000 Aarhus C

International applicant?

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Please find more information here: https://internationalstaff.au.dk/relocationservice/

Please find more information about research opportunities at Aarhus University here: http://international.au.dk/research/

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here: 
http://talent.au.dk/junior-researcher-development-programme/

Terms of employment

Salary and terms of employment are governed by the Cirkulære om overenskomst for akademikere i staten  (in Danish). You will be employed as postdoctoral fellow at base pay level 4–8 with additional supplements in accordance with the Cirkulære om protokollat om visse ansættelsesvilkår for videnskabeligt personale ved universiteter (in Danish).

The job content and qualification requirements are described in further detail in the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

Application procedure

When you apply for this position it is mandatory to attach the following:

• 
Application

• 
Curriculum Vitae. You are encouraged to declare any periods of leave without research activity, including, for example, maternity leave, since your research activities are assessed in relation to your actual research time

• 
Education (diploma for master's, PhD and possibly higher doctoral degree)

• 
List of publications (the enclosed publications must be clearly marked on the list of publications)

• 
Publications. Up to three publications can be included in the application. In the event of several authors the publications must be accompanied by a co-author statement concerning the applicant's share of the collaborative work with the consent of the co-authors. This template may be used for the purpose

Materials which cannot be uploaded together with the application may be submitted in three copies to Aarhus BSS HR & PhD, Aarhus University, Bartholins Allé 16, DK-8000 Aarhus C.

jobs.occupation: Four-year Researcher position on Greenland marine ecosystems
jobs.description:
Four-year Researcher position on Greenland marine ecosystems
The Department of Ecoscience, Aarhus University, invites applications for a four-year scientist position on the biodiversity and coastal ecosystem status and trends along Greenland’s coast with a special focus on the use of eDNA for monitoring of marine macroalgae. The position is linked to multiple international projects, including the Greenland Ecosystem Monitoring Programme with an overarching theme of studying the impacts of climate change on coastal ecosystems in Greenland. The position requires active participation in developing and attracting funding for new projects including a special focus on developing and implementing eDNA tools for the ecological research and monitoring.

This is a four–year position available from 15 February 2027. 

Job description
The position focuses on the ecology of coastal marine ecosystems in Greenland and their responses to climate change, particularly warming and the ongoing loss of the cryosphere.

You are expected to participate in annual field campaigns in Greenland and contribute to the analysis and interpretation of monitoring and experimental data from coastal Greenland ecosystems. A particular focus will be on developing and applying environmental DNA (eDNA) methods for characterising and quantifying marine biodiversity, with an emphasis on marine macroalgae. This includes establishing high-quality biodiversity baselines and improving our capacity to detect changes in species distributions and the arrival of new species.

Your profile
Applicants must hold a PhD in biology or a closely related field. Documented experience with Arctic marine vegetation and ecosystem ecology is considered an advantage, together with expertise in eDNA-based approaches, including metabarcoding, quantitative PCR-based methods such as digital PCR (dPCR), bioinformatics and biostatistics.

Experience with marine fieldwork, DNA barcoding, experimental design and morphological species identification is also an advantage. The successful candidate is expected to have experience in developing research ideas and in contributing to research proposals and grant applications. A scientific diving certification is considered an advantage.

Fluency in spoken and written English is required. In addition, the candidate should enjoy working collaboratively in an interdisciplinary and international research environment and be motivated to contribute actively to fieldwork, research development and scientific publication.

Who we are
The Department of Ecoscience (https://ecos.au.dk/en/) is organised under the Faculty of Technical Sciences. The department’s research areas cover most aspects of biology and ecology, spanning all biological levels from genetics, physiological processes, individuals, populations and species to entire ecosystems. Strategic and applied research account for a large part of the research activities at the Department of Ecoscience. Geographically, the department works from the tropics to the poles, but with greater focus on Danish conditions. The department has an obligation towards the Ministry of Environment and Food of Denmark and the authorities in Greenland as national advisors on environmental issues. The department’s research, consultancy and teaching are linked to strong and active research groups. 

What we offer 
The successful candidate is offered:

• Access to a well-developed research infrastructure
• Office space and shared equipment
• a research climate inviting lively, open and critical discussion within and across different fields of research
• a working environment with teamwork, close working relations, network activities among young scientists and social activities
• a workplace characterized by professionalism, equality and a healthy work-life balance
Place of work and area of employment 
The place of work is the main University campus in Aarhus, C.F. Møllers Allé 3, 8000 Aarhus C. 

Contact information

For further information, please contact Mikael Sejr (mse@ecos.au.dk) or Dorte Krause-Jensen (dkj@ecos.au.dk). 

Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the assessment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. The selection is made on the basis of an assessment of who of the candidates are most relevant considering the requirements of the advertisement. All applicants will be notified within 6 weeks whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee and will receive his/her assessment. 

Formalities and salary range 
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

• Engage with equipment owners, IT, engineering and operational stakeholders to understand system requirements and ensure utility availability is aligned with their delivery schedules.

• Provide informed technical recommendations, support decision-making and escalate matters affecting cost, scope or programme timelines through established governance processes.

• Contribute to the successful handover of utility systems to the operational and maintenance organisations.

• Collaborate across the wider project team, supporting other critical workstreams where priorities and project needs require.

• This is a project manager position rather than a detailed engineering design role.

Qualifications

To succeed in this role, you will bring a strong technical foundation in utility systems, practical experience in regulated operational environments and the ability to manage complex engineering activities.

We are particularly interested in candidates who have developed their careers through technical, maintenance, facilities or operational engineering roles before progressing into project management.

We expect you to have:

• A relevant educational background in engineering or a related technical discipline, or equivalent practical industry experience.

• Strong technical experience in either clean utilities or industrial utilities, particularly piping related systems such as purified water, clean steam, heating, cooling, water distribution or compressed air.

• Demonstrable experience in equipment or systems commissioning, qualification and/or validation, including a sound understanding of controlled processes, documentation and operational requirements.

• Practical experience working within an operational plant, manufacturing facility or similarly complex technical environment, including exposure to maintenance activities, system start ups, shutdowns or equipment qualification.

• Proven experience coordinating engineering projects, technical workstreams, contractors or specialist service providers.

Experience working within regulated or process driven industries where safety, quality, documentation and controlled operating procedures are essential.

• Strong planning, coordination and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and technical dependencies.

• The ability to communicate effectively in English, both written and spoken.

• Experience in pharmaceutical manufacturing, biotechnology or other GMP regulated environments would be advantageous but is not essential.

• We also welcome relevant experience from industries such as food and beverage, chemical manufacturing, oil and gas, and engineering or EPC organisations, provided you bring the necessary utilities and qualification expertise.

• Experience across both clean and industrial utilities would be beneficial; however, strong expertise in either discipline is sufficient.

• Knowledge of Science and Risk-Based Validation (SRV), commissioning and qualification methodologies, and large-scale CAPEX or Greenfield projects would also be advantageous.

About the department

• You will join the DPM Expansion Future QC programme in Hillerod, where we are delivering a major new quality control laboratory facility to support Novo's expanding manufacturing capabilities.

• The programme involves the development of approximately 42,000 m² of new laboratory and supporting infrastructure, representing a significant investment in the future of our quality control operations.

• The project is currently progressing through construction, with commissioning, qualification and phased handover activities forming critical elements of the delivery programme.

• Our engineering organisation is relatively lean, bringing together specialists across utilities, validation, engineering, technical interfaces and other essential project disciplines.

• This structure provides an opportunity for individuals to take genuine ownership of their responsibilities, work closely with experienced colleagues and influence important technical and operational decisions.

We value collaboration, practical problem solving and the willingness to take responsibility. While you will lead your own workstream, you will also be part of a team that supports one another and responds flexibly as project priorities evolve.

Joining us means contributing to a technically challenging Greenfield project where your experience, judgement and decisions will make a visible difference.

About you

• You are an experienced technical professional who combines a strong understanding of utility systems with the ability to plan, coordinate and deliver complex project activities.

• You understand what it takes to commission, qualify and operate technical systems in real world environments, and you appreciate the importance of controlled procedures, thorough planning and effective communication.

• You are comfortable working with experienced engineering specialists and contractors, asking the right questions, challenging assumptions constructively and bringing stakeholders together to find practical solutions.

• You take ownership of your responsibilities and are confident making recommendations, while recognising when issues require wider discussion or escalation.

• You are also adaptable and pragmatic.

• You understand that priorities can change within major construction programmes and are willing to support colleagues and other workstreams when needed.

• Above all, you enjoy being close to the technical and operational realities of a project and take pride in helping complex systems move successfully from construction through qualification and into operation.

Why Novo

At Novo, we don't wait for change. We drive it. Our commitment to defeating serious chronic diseases is built on more than a century of innovation, collaboration and a determination to make a meaningful difference to people's lives.

Joining our Future QC expansion programme offers the opportunity to contribute to a major investment in our manufacturing and quality control capabilities, while developing your experience within a global organisation undertaking complex engineering and expansion projects.

You will have the opportunity to work alongside experienced professionals, influence the delivery of a significant Greenfield development and contribute to infrastructure that will support our operations for years to come.

Working at Novo

Every day, we seek the solutions that defeat serious chronic diseases. To do this, we approach our work with an unconventional spirit, a determination to innovate and a commitment to creating lasting change.

Working at Novo means joining a global healthcare company where talented people collaborate across disciplines, challenge established thinking and pursue solutions that can improve the lives of millions.

When you join us, you're not just starting a job you're becoming part of a story that spans generations.

Salary and benefits

The salary range for this position is DKK 742,600 to DKK 1,091,600 per year, depending on experience and qualifications.

Incentives and benefits

Novo offers a competitive compensation package, including pension, bonus opportunities and a range of employee benefits designed to support your professional and personal wellbeing.

What we offer

There is, of course, more on offer here than the uniqueness of our culture and the extraordinary results we produce.

We offer an environment where you can develop professionally, take on meaningful challenges and build your career within a global organisation committed to innovation and long term progress.

Our benefits are designed with your career and life stage in mind, supporting your professional development, wellbeing and work-life balance.

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

At Novo, we're not chasing quick fixes we're creating lasting change for long term health. For over 100 years, we've been driven by a single purpose: to defeat serious chronic diseases and help millions of people live healthier lives.

This dedication fuels our constant curiosity and inspires us to explore new possibilities, challenge conventions and push the boundaries of what is possible.

Together, we're life changing.

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

jobs.occupation: Project Manager
jobs.description:
Your impact begins here

As Project Manager, you will help the VP of People Relations turn complex people and business priorities into clear decisions, aligned action and measurable progress. You will advise, challenge assumptions and lead selected cross-functional initiatives from definition to adoption, freeing the VP to focus on leadership and enterprise impact. Your work will help priority people initiatives land well, supporting the colleagues who serve people living with serious chronic diseases.

What you’ll bring

You are a structured, trusted thinker who can turn complexity into practical recommendations and keep things moving across organisational boundaries.

• At least 5 years’ experience in HR project management or a similar role.

• Experience leading cross-functional projects from planning through implementation.

• Experience preparing concise, decision-ready material for senior leaders.

• Strong business understanding, analytical skills and sound judgement in turning complex issues into practical recommendations.

• The ability to navigate complexity and ambiguity while ensuring progress.

• Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to influence delivery without formal authority.

• A proactive approach, sound prioritisation and disciplined follow-through.

• Discretion, and the confidence to challenge constructively and raise issues respectfully.

• Professional fluency in English.

• A relevant master’s degree and experience from a people function, consulting or working closely with a senior leader are advantages, but not essential.

• Familiarity with global employee relations and labour law is helpful, alongside the ability to work effectively with subject-matter specialists.

What you’ll do

You will prepare, align and follow through so that decisions turn into results. In your first year, success means the VP receives timely, concise decision material, selected initiatives reach agreed milestones with evidence of adoption, and risks and delays are raised early.

• Advise the VP as a trusted partner on agreed priorities: challenge assumptions, develop options and recommend practical next steps.

• Turn complex topics into concise briefings, presentations and decision material, including positions, anticipated questions and draft messages for the VP’s review.

• Keep an overview of priorities, initiatives and upcoming decisions, and recommend what to prioritise, defer, simplify or stop.

• Anticipate emerging issues and escalate material risks or delays early, with an assessment of impact and a recommended response.

• Lead selected cross-functional people initiatives and on-going tasks from definition through implementation, adoption and follow-up, with agreed outcomes, owners and milestones.

• Secure accountable owners and deadlines, track progress and outcomes, and represent the VP in selected discussions where explicitly delegated.

Who you’ll work with

You will report to the VP of People Relations and be part of the People Relations leadership team based in Bagsværd, Denmark.

Your closest partners will be the VP and leadership team, PO Business Partners and relevant global Centres of Excellence. You will also work with enterprise stakeholders and project teams across functions and countries, connecting local needs with global expertise.

You will work hand in hand with the VP’s Personal Assistant, who manages daily executive support and leadership routines. Together you will coordinate planning and keep ownership clear, so work moves forward with clarity and pace.

What you can expect here

You will work close to senior leadership, with the trust to act independently within an agreed mandate and a voice in how priorities are shaped. You will build new skills by leading initiatives across functions and countries, and you will be supported to perform at your best, with clear expectations and honest feedback.

Salary

For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from  651,000.00 to 956,900.00 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position.

The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area, and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here.

Start now

Your impact begins today. Apply for the Project Manager role by 31st October 2026. We review applications on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

jobs.occupation: Head of the Nordic-Baltic Cyber Consortium (NBCC)
jobs.description:
About the position
The Danish Resilience Agency (SAMSIK) is seeking a highly experienced and strategic leader to serve as Head of the Nordic-Baltic Cyber Consortium (NBCC).

The NBCC is a Danish-hosted, EU-supported cybersecurity initiative established under the EU Cyber Solidarity Act. The consortium brings together Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Iceland, Latvia, Lithuania and Norway to build and operate a regional cyber hub that strengthens situational awareness and analytical capacity across the Nordic-Baltic region.

As Head of the NBCC, you will be responsible for establishing and leading a new international organisation of strategic importance to both regional and European cybersecurity. While formally employed by the Danish Resilience Agency, you will report to the NBCC Executive Board, composed of senior representatives from the participating national cybersecurity authorities, and operate in close coordination with EU institutions.

The position is based in Copenhagen, Denmark.

Key responsibilities

Strategic leadership and governance

• 
Provide overall strategic direction and leadership of the NBCC in line with EU objectives, consortium agreements and national mandates.

• 
Develop, implement and continuously adjust the NBCC’s strategic roadmap, including the phased build-up from initial deployment to full operational capability.

• 
Ensure alignment between the NBCC activities, EU cybersecurity policies and the strategic interests of participating member states.

Management, organisation and budget

• 
Act as head of the NBCC organisation, including direct line management of up to eight permanent staff based in Denmark and professional oversight of national analysts located in each participating member state.

• 
Build and lead a cohesive multinational organisation with a shared operational culture, while managing differing national frameworks and practices.

• 
Ensure sound financial management, reporting and documentation in accordance with EU and national requirements.

Operational responsibility

• 
Hold overall responsibility for the NBCC’s operational delivery, including the secure and reliable operation of platforms for cyber threat intelligence sharing, analytical collaboration and communication.

• 
Ensure structured and timely sharing of relevant cyber threat information and contribution to regional and European situational awareness.

About you
To succeed in this role, we expect that you:

• 
Have proven experience leading multinational or international cooperation involving multiple stakeholders and governance layers; experience from Nordic-Baltic cooperation is a strong advantage.

• 
Possess a strong understanding of cyber threat intelligence, incident response ecosystems and information-sharing mechanisms at national and international level.

• 
Have demonstrated experience with EU cooperation, preferably including EU-funded projects and engagement with EU institutions.

• 
Are able to operate confidently at senior political and administrative levels, nationally and internationally.

• 
Can demonstrate strong regional insight and experience, for example from a Nordic or Baltic cybersecurity authority or a comparable organisation.

 In addition, you:

• 
Exercise strong strategic judgement and are able to balance political, operational and technical considerations.

• 
Have excellent leadership and communication skills and are able to build trust across national and organisational boundaries.

• 
Are fully proficient in English; knowledge of one or more Nordic or Baltic languages is an advantage. Danish language skills are not required.

About the Danish Resilience Agency
The Danish Resilience Agency is under the authority of the Danish Ministry for Resilience and Preparedness. The agency is responsible for tasks related to cybersecurity, crisis management, physical security and protection of critical infrastructure.

We advise and support authorities, companies and key societal functions in preventing and managing incidents and crises. The agency currently employs approximately 300 staff members working across disciplines in a highly engaged and mission-driven environment.

About the NBCC
The NBCC is a Nordic-Baltic cybersecurity cooperation supported by the EU. Through the NBCC, the participating countries jointly establish and operate a regional cyber hub that enhances collective situational awareness and analytical capacity.

The NBCC will jointly procure cybersecurity capabilities with the EU, employ analysts in Copenhagen and across the member states, and contribute to the European Cybersecurity Shield. The NBCC is organised as a distinct entity within the Danish Resilience Agency and is accountable to its Executive Board.

As Head of the NBCC, you will be responsible for building this organisation from the ground up and for strengthening collective regional resilience against cyber threats.

Salary and terms of employment
Salary and terms of employment will depend on qualifications and experience and will be determined in accordance with the collective agreements applicable to employees in the Danish state. The area of employment is the Danish Ministry for Resilience and Preparedness.

Employment is conditional on obtaining and maintaining a Danish security clearance at SECRET (DK: HEMMELIGT) level for the duration of employment.

The position is a fixed-term appointment for a period of 4 years, with the possibility of extension.

The position is full-time 37-hours per week, and the duty station is Holsteinsgade 63, 2100 Copenhagen.

To be eligible for employment EU/EEA Citizens are required to obtain an EU residence document as proof of your right to reside and work in Denmark. Non-EU/EEA Citizens must hold a valid residence and work permit before you can begin working in Denmark. Citizens of Sweden, Norway, Finland, or Iceland do not require a residence or work permit to live and work in Denmark. For more detailed information regarding the regulations for your specific citizenship, please visit: New to Denmark and/or Info Norden | Nordisk Samarbejde

If the position is filled by an applicant not currently residing in Denmark, the Danish Resilience Agency is prepared to offer a relocation package of up to 45.000 DKK. Any other costs related to relocation or housing must be covered by the employee.

Are you interested?
Please submit your application via the “Apply” button on this page. Your application must be received by the recruitment system no later than 15th November 2026 and must include a CV and relevant diplomas of education.

For further information about the position, please contact Kia Slæbæk Jensen at +45 2134 1851 or Morten Bro at +45 2178 4257.

All qualified applicants are encouraged to apply regardless of personal background.

Applications may be shared with participants from the employment committee from all participating countries.
